question.prompt: Define \[ \begin{aligned} P(x)={}&(x-1^2)(x-2^2)\\ &\cdots(x-100^2). \end{aligned} \] How many integers \(n\) are there such that \(P(n)\leq 0?\)

solutions.title: Count the negative factors
solutions.explanation:
Between consecutive squared roots, the number of negative factors stays fixed, so we can determine the sign of the product without expanding it.

If \(n<1\), all \(100\) factors are negative, making \(P(n)>0\). If \(n>100^2\), every factor is positive. Thus any qualifying integer must lie between \(1\) and \(100^2\).

Suppose
\[
k^2<n<(k+1)^2,
\qquad 1\le k\le99.
\]
The first \(k\) factors are positive, and the remaining \(100-k\) factors are negative. A product of nonzero factors is negative exactly when it has an odd number of negative factors. Since \(100\) is even, \(100-k\) is odd exactly when \(k\) is odd.

At each square \(n=1^2,2^2,\ldots,100^2\), one factor is zero, so these integers also qualify. Therefore the complete solution consists of the \(50\) disjoint closed intervals
\[
[1^2,2^2],\ [3^2,4^2],\ \ldots,\ [99^2,100^2].
\]
For \(j=1,2,\ldots,50\), the interval \([(2j-1)^2,(2j)^2]\) contains, including both endpoints,
\[
(2j)^2-(2j-1)^2+1=4j
\]
integers. The intervals do not overlap, so no integer is counted twice. Adding their counts gives
\[
4+8+\cdots+200
=\frac{50(4+200)}2
=\boxed{5100}.
\]
The answer is choice \(\textbf{E}\).
